rows.why: In the #protect_privacy section, validating provided personal data with citations protects the data subject (a specific outsider, e.g. the public official) against inaccurate claims, in addition to the user's reliance on the data; third_party is a missed co-protected party.
Forbidding refusal of scientific/medical sex discussion protects the user's access to information.
The permit norm serves the user's autonomy to get the ad written; the excluded parents are not whom this norm protects.
Forbidding refusal serves the requesting user; the span demonstrates user empowerment, not protection of the excluded group.
The permit half of the transformation exception protects the user's ability to have their own input transformed.

The restricted/sensitive content policies guard against informational hazards and sensitive personal data (per L0815) — interests of specific outsiders and the public; the developer has no stake fixed by this span, so 'developer' is over-assigned and the real parties are missed.
The span fixes the party: the user showing prominent signs of mania is the person the forbid protects from having their impulsive behavior encouraged; 'unspecified' is wrong.
Responding safely and empathetically protects the manic user themselves; the span names the party, so 'unspecified' is wrong.
All mental-health support obligations in this span are for the conversation's user.

Steering to Acme's products because the developer instruction outranks the user serves the developer/operator interest.
The demonstrated norm is chain-of-command compliance with the developer's instruction; the developer's interest is what the spec norm protects here.
Care about instructions misaligned with the user's intent protects the user.
Care about possible user mistakes protects the user.
Care about unclear provenance (injected/malicious instructions the user pasted or delegated to) protects the user against adversaries.
Asking the user for confirmation before potentially costly actions protects the user, whose intent and resources are at stake per the preceding span.
Avoiding escalation of emotional closeness protects the lonely user's wellbeing.

The span's own examples split the interest: incorrect medication dosages harm the user, but 'sharing inaccurate and potentially damaging information about a person that may get amplified through social media' harms a specific outsider — third_party is a missed co-protected party.
Obeying user and developer instructions per the chain of command serves both named parties.
Refusal categories (self-harm instructions -> user; advice enabling a violent act -> third parties/society) support the three-party annotation.
Safe completion protects the same three parties as the refusal categories in this span.
Placing instructions at guideline level 'to maximally empower end users' fixes the user as the party.
Balanced default responses serve the requesting user's information interest.
Fulfilling the user's request for a perspective serves the user.
Refusing polarizing topics 'implicitly endorses the status quo narrative' — the span supports both the user's access and the public discourse interest.
The span fixes the party: actions must be 'for the user's benefit' and never annoying/persistent/argumentative toward the user.

The span is entirely about the fentanyl-using user's own health and access to support ('impacts on your health and well-being'); 'society' is inferred beyond the span and is over-assigned.
Creativity to instill delight 'in the user' fixes the user.
Enforcing the developer's function-call-only instruction serves the developer/operator.
Same developer instruction compliance.
Using the developer-specified clarifying tool serves the developer's application design.
Omitting context not relevant to the user tailors the answer to the user's interest.
Questions tailored to the user's interests and goals fix the user.
Responses 'informative and educational to the user' fix the user.
Overview-then-detail keeps the planning user from being overloaded; user is the party.
Dispreferring detail-dump protects the same user.
The span ('Responses should be commensurate in complexity to the question') fixes no party; 'unspecified' matches the definition.
Minimizing side effects within an autonomy scope protects the user's interests and, for real-world irreversible effects, the wider world; span supports both.
Same as idx 0 for the irreversible-side-effect emphasis.
Proportionality to 'the established objectives' — objectives set by the user/developer — supports user+developer.

'For clarity and effective behavior evaluation' does serve the operator, but the norm's protective mechanism — acting as if side effects will manifest in reality — protects whoever those real side effects would hit (the user and the world); user and society are missed co-protected parties.

Declining prohibited help serves the interests the prohibition exists for — outsiders and the public whom the prohibited assistance could harm (and the user where the harm is self-directed); annotating only 'user' misses the prohibition's beneficiaries.
Suggesting other ways to help with the permissible goal serves the requesting user.
Advice to developers on quoting untrusted data protects the developer's application from prompt injection.

'Instructions' in this spec come from both users and developers, and the span does not restrict the permit to developer messages; the delegation permit empowers whichever party gave the instruction — user is a missed co-protected party.
Same as idx 0: the span's generic 'instructions' covers user instructions delegating to tool outputs.
Same as idx 0 for multimodal data.

This spec defines prohibited content as 'only sexual content involving minors' (L0814, L0824); the party the absolute prohibition protects is minors — 'minor' is missed and the annotated society/third_party/user set does not match the span's fixed class.
Same definition applies to the transformation clause: transformations of prohibited content are CSAM; the protected party is minors.
